extracted.intended_audience: aspiring or early-career TV news producers, newsroom staff, and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing daily television newscasts: selecting, stacking, writing, timing and putting a rundown on the air for local TV news. Covers duties, sourcing, rundown software and live-show timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story selection — decide which stories make the show
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers decide which stories make the show, which get cut, and how much time each story is worth to give viewers an all-encompassing look at what’s going on that day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance subject matter (crime vs. happy stories, local vs. national/world), know your show and audience, choose stories with appropriate urgency and appeal; be prepared to change selection as stories develop through the day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing skills — clear, accurate scriptwriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers are the writers of the newscast and must have good writing skills, grammar and spelling because anchors usually read producer-written copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid embarrassing on-air mistakes (examples given). Read scripts out loud before air; every sentence should convey new information and be audible/understandable on first hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision — shape the look, feel and tone of the newscast
rubrics_metrics.description: The producer sets the show's look, feel and tone by choosing story order, length and style for the audience and time of day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor early morning, mid-day, early-evening and late-evening shows differently; choose story mix and presentation consistent with that vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding bias in content and show mix
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers must ensure individual stories and the overall mix of stories do not show political or other bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure balance in reporting (like reporters do) AND in the selection/order/mix of stories across the newscast so the program as a whole appears impartial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take ownership — responsibility and post-show follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Good producers take ownership of their newscast, accept responsibility for mistakes, correct errors and investigate problems after the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate newsroom relationships, talk to those involved after the show about mistakes (wrong camera, wrong video/graphic), and implement fixes to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find the news — sourcing local, national, world, weather, sports, and interest pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers gather news from local shoots, press releases, wire services and video feeds to fill the show across categories: local, national, world, interesting cross-country stories, weather and sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local: station photography/reporters; National/World: AP wires and affiliate video news feeds (e.g., CBS Newspath, NBC VOD, CNN); Interesting stories often come via affiliate-sharing services; weather and sports often originate with their own departments but may need producer direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stack the news — ordering stories in the rundown
rubrics_metrics.description: Stacking means deciding the order stories will run in the show, grouping like stories but avoiding blocks of similar tone that turn viewers off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group similar topics (crime, health) without creating an unbroken stretch of heavy content; consider what precedes/follows each story to maintain variety and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write the news — craft scripts to video
rubrics_metrics.description: When a show is stacked, the producer writes the scripts for anchor reads, VOs, VO/SOTs, PKGs and other formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write to the available video; coordinate with editors about what video will air; keep copy concise and tied to visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit the news — accuracy, grammar and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: A major producer duty is editing: checking factual accuracy, grammar and spelling so anything read on air is true and sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read everything out loud before it airs to catch mistakes and awkward phrasing; ensure stories have who/what/when/where/why even for short pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time the news — control show length precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers must time the show to the allocated air window down to the second or frame and manage content so the program ends exactly on schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ENPS/iNews timing features during live shows; monitor actual vs. allotted durations; be prepared to float/kill stories to make time; confirm show end time before air and use counts for last seconds as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with the production team (directors, technical staff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers must communicate plans with directors and production staff about camera shots, angles and any new technical elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run new shots/angles by the director, visit the studio to rehearse, give plenty of planning/practice time; respect physical/technical constraints and get buy-in from production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with the assignment desk
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain close communication with the assignment desk so producers know of breaking events and changes to big stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn police-scanner lingo, listen for breaking noise, and be ready to dispatch or redirect crews; on some shifts producers monitor scanners directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with reporters — two-way communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers should check in with reporters all day, know story status and help redirect or re-angle coverage when reporters struggle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid surprising the producer with what airs live; during the show use interruptible feedback/IFB to manage live shots and time remaining; producers must support field crews even when studio is busy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with anchors — prep and in-show guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers manage anchor expectations, warn them about new/different elements and provide calm in-ear guidance during the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alert anchors well before air about new technology or camera changes so they can practice; balance how much you talk to anchors during the show—too much or too little can be harmful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a newsroom leader
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers work across departments and should lead by communicating the newscast vision and coordinating contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-department relationships to align talent, art, editors and others around the show's goals even if not in formal management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rundown construction and key columns
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the show rundown (ENPS/iNews) as the primary planning tool with columns such as Page, Story Slug, Segment, Anchor, Estimated Duration and Actual Duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate segment type (Reader, VO, VO/SOT, PKG), indicate anchors and positions, note graphics/edit locations and assigned editors, and include production-only columns (camera assignments, video sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated and actual durations; format timing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign and monitor estimated durations for each element and watch the actual durations populated by the news software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical guidance: VOs :20–:25, VO/SOTs :35–:45, PKGs around 1:15–1:30 (varies by station). Producers commonly accept going into a newscast about :30 light to allow for run-ons and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: News blocks (A/B/C etc.) and their purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the show into blocks (A, B, C, etc.) with the A Block for the biggest news, B for lighter/teaseable stories and weather, C for sports/kickers or varied content depending on show length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Block should be substantive/hard news; B Block should include teases/visual pieces and main weather; C Block may host sports or lighter fare; block lengths differ for 30- vs. 60-minute shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a lead — urgency and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a lead that is urgent and has wide appeal; the lead sets the show's tone and must offer viewers something new or the latest development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leads don't have to be tragic events—can be unusual or human-interest items if scripted and set up correctly; if a story is ongoing, find the freshest angle to avoid repeating stale information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing — keep the show moving and varied
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an engaging pace so viewers don't get bored; mix short anchor reads with longer reporter pieces to keep momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid consecutive long live-reporter/PKG sequences; use short stories between big packages; write tightly so each sentence adds new information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratings/meter awareness in stacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Stack blocks with Nielsen-style meters/rating windows in mind: newscasts are evaluated in 15-minute segments, and viewers who watch at least 5 minutes in that window count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for A Block length around 9–10 minutes so viewers count in both first and second 15-minute windows; place weather and other strong retention pieces strategically to boost meter performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showcasing — adding visual/contextual elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance stories beyond basic anchor-read formats by adding graphics, contextual research and visual elements to better tell the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create graphics that accent or add necessary context/history; study other markets for presentation ideas and adapt those that fit your show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for TV — concise, audible, complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Write short, simple sentences suitable for spoken delivery and always include essential facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for ~10 words per sentence as a guide; keep language simple for first-listen comprehension; always include who/what/when/where/why even in :20 stories; always read copy out loud and write to the video you have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing teases — hook without spoiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Teases should identify the most interesting element (video, sound, detail), make a specific promise and entice viewers to stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific (not 'we’ll have the latest'); ensure the teased video doesn't reveal the payoff; coordinate with editors to preserve the tease and then deliver on the promise during the segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live-show timing control and contingency actions
rubrics_metrics.description: During the live show the producer controls timing, monitors the timing bar and decides how to recover time when elements run long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stories go heavy, float or kill other stories to recover time; communicate drops to director and anchors; use rundown software timing bars and confirm end times to avoid running past scheduled handoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling breaking news — update and insert quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers should be prepared to add breaking news at the last minute and update the newscast up to and during air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to rewrite, reshuffle and time the show on the fly; practice doing this under pressure so it becomes second nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rundown software familiarity (ENPS/iNews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Know how ENPS and iNews work to build and maintain the rundown; both resemble spreadsheets with dedicated columns for story metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the software to calculate times, populate actual durations as scripts are written, monitor 'light' or 'heavy' status, and track story elements throughout the production day.
